author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it. It is reachable by its address alone, with no navigation entry and no link from another page.
acceptance_criteria: Opening GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows, by its stored name, on one page with no pagination.
Each specialty is listed with the veterinarians holding it, each veterinarian shown by first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page; the page lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster.
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian shown against it.
The specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one.
No navigation entry and no link on any other page of the system leads to the specialty directory.
The page itself carries the standard navigation to owner search and to the veterinarian directory, as every page does (REQ-SYS-001).
Every piece of new user-facing wording on the page is drawn from the supported-language wording rather than fixed into the page, and is present in every supported language (REQ-LANG-002).
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged by the owner's decision)
A navigation entry or a link from another page to the specialty directory
Searching or filtering within the specialty directory
notes: Minted from intake-decision REQ-SPECIALTYDIRECTORY-001 (handoff.jsonl line 1); REQ-SPEC-001 follows the docs/prd.md prefix convention. Owner stated the address verbatim as "GET /specialties.html"; the PRD prose keeps it out as mechanism, so this record carries it. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Open questions the intake left deliberately open, recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions rather than blocked on: (1) which stable order the specialties and their veterinarians take; (2) whether a specialty no veterinarian holds should be marked as unheld — narrowest reading taken, listed with nothing under it; (3) whether NG-9 (no veterinarian search) reads against this page — recorded unchanged, since the page offers no search and lists everything. The last two acceptance criteria are conformance with standing requirements REQ-SYS-001 and REQ-LANG-002, not owner statements.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice lands entirely inside the existing vet feature package; no new package, no new dependency, no new bounded context. Two things are genuinely new. First, the page must list a specialty no veterinarian holds, which no current read path can return: VetRepository is typed Repository<Vet,Integer>, so a SpecialtyRepository is required. PetTypeRepository is the exact precedent for a name-ordered lookup repository. Second, the Vet-to-Specialty association is mapped one way only, so the directory's content has to be derived by inverting it. Where that derivation lives is a real decision, because docs/architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog admits no business rule in a web controller and states the existing controller rules do not extend to new ones. Recorded in ADR 2026-08-21 read-side-view-model-for-the-specialty-directory: the derivation is an immutable SpecialtyDirectory value object carrying displayed names, built by a static factory from a specialty collection and a veterinarian collection, unit-testable with real objects and no Spring context. docs/system-design.md Contracts now carries SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectory, and SpecialtyController against REQ-SPEC-001, each marked designed and not yet in the code.
integration_points: New GET route /specialties.html on a new package-private SpecialtyController in the vet package. The prd-entry file_targets name VetController; a separate controller is the better fit and matches the one-controller-per-domain-noun precedent (OwnerController, PetController, VisitController in one package). It also keeps the existing @WebMvcTest(VetController.class) slice free of a second mocked repository.

SpecialtyRepository reads every specialty, so an unheld specialty is present in the result. VetRepository.findAll() supplies the veterinarians and keeps its existing @Cacheable("vets") behavior unchanged.

The specialty read is deliberately uncached: a second cache would have to be declared in system/CacheConfiguration.java and would widen the unresolved vet-cache eviction question (system-design.md Open Question 5).
specialtyList.html uses fragments/layout.html like every other page, which satisfies REQ-SYS-001 navigation. No menuItem is added to layout.html and no other template links to the route.

New message keys must be added to all eleven bundles under src/main/resources/messages/; I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build otherwise. Existing keys (specialties, name, none) are reusable where the wording matches.

patterns.description: lookup-value repository returning rows in name order via an explicit @Query; the shape SpecialtyRepository follows
Value object (in force) for SpecialtyDirectory; Web controller (in force) bounds SpecialtyController to bind-delegate-select
getSpecialties() already sorts by name; the same name ordering is the stable order for the directory

risks.risk: SpecialtyDirectory holding Specialty and Vet entities would make a value object wrap mutable framework-mapped types, weakening equality-by-value and pulling in the persistence-entity exception unnecessarily.
risks.mitigation: Carry only the names the page shows (specialty name; veterinarian first and last name). The page displays nothing else, so nothing is lost and the closed value-object properties hold in full.

risks.risk: Passing 'vets' as the layout fragment's menu argument would highlight the veterinarian directory nav entry, implying a navigation relationship the acceptance criteria deny.
risks.mitigation: Pass a menu value matching no menuItem in fragments/layout.html so no entry is marked active.

risks.risk: The stable-order choice is an open product question in docs/prd.md, so an arbitrary order could be shipped and later contradicted.
risks.mitigation: ADR 2026-08-21 fixes it as specialty name order, veterinarians by last name then first name, matching PetTypeRepository and Vet.getSpecialties(). The acceptance criterion requires only stability, so this is decidable at design level.

risks.risk: Derivation drifting into SpecialtyController would be a fresh breach of the Web controller row, not covered by the recorded existing deviation.
risks.mitigation: The controller reads both repositories, calls the SpecialtyDirectory factory, and selects the view. Any grouping, filtering, or sorting logic belongs in SpecialtyDirectory.

notes: Test placement: the four content criteria (every specialty on one page, holders by first and last name, veterinarians holding no specialty absent, a specialty no veterinarian holds still listed, stable order) are all decidable against SpecialtyDirectory with real objects and no framework context. Put them in SpecialtyDirectoryTests; keep SpecialtyControllerTests to the MockMvc concerns (route resolves, view name, model attribute, rendered page). Security: the route is read-only and adds no trust boundary beyond the project's documented unauthenticated posture (system-design.md Security Context); rendered names are user-supplied only via seed data and Thymeleaf escaping applies as elsewhere. No secrets, no parameters, no query input on this route. Docs written this dispatch: docs/adr/2026-08-21-read-side-view-model-for-the-specialty-directory.md (new, indexed in docs/adr/README.md); docs/system-design.md Contracts rows plus the read-side value-object rule, the vet package-tree line, a provenance clause for designed statements, and a cross-reference on Open Question 2. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. docs/prd.md untouched.

The controller declares no @InitBinder because it binds no command object.

title: Specialty directory
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it. It is reachable by its address alone, with no navigation entry and no link from another page.
acceptance_criteria: Opening GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows, by its stored name, on one page with no pagination.
Each specialty is listed with the veterinarians holding it, each veterinarian shown by first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page; the page lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster.
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian shown against it.
The specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one.
No navigation entry and no link on any other page of the system leads to the specialty directory.
The page itself carries the standard navigation to owner search and to the veterinarian directory, as every page does (REQ-SYS-001).
Every piece of new user-facing wording on the page is drawn from the supported-language wording rather than fixed into the page, and is present in every supported language (REQ-LANG-002).
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged by the owner's decision)
A navigation entry or a link from another page to the specialty directory
Searching or filtering within the specialty directory

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Thirteen files in one module, twenty-one hunks, and every production hunk is a new file: SpecialtyController, SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectory, and specialtyList.html add a route with zero deletions from existing production code. The only edits to existing files are an additive test in ClinicServiceTests and four docs. No sensitive paths, no build files, no dependency change, no shared code modified, so nothing already shipping can regress.

semantic_surprise.note: Read the derivation, the template, and the repository query line by line and nothing does more than it claims. SpecialtyDirectory inverts the one-way Vet-to-Specialty mapping by grouping holder display names under specialty names, keeps an entry for an unheld specialty via getOrDefault, and drops a veterinarian holding nothing because the flatMap starts from the vet's specialty set. The apparent first-name/last-name mismatch is not one: display is first-then-last, sort is last-then-first, deliberately. distinct() was removed on purpose so a duplicate stored name is not silently collapsed. The template passes a layout menu argument matching no menuItem, so no navigation entry is marked active, uses th:text only with no th:utext, and the eager Vet-to-Specialty fetch means the open-in-view=false setting cannot bite. One cosmetic residual: an unheld specialty renders the reused none message key rather than an empty cell, where the PRD open question describes listing it with nothing under it. It mirrors vetList.html exactly and satisfies the criterion as written.

test_adequacy.note: The tests are real, not tautological. Seven unit tests drive SpecialtyDirectory with real domain objects and no Spring context, asserting containsExactly on ordering including a last-name tie-break, so a broken sort fails them. Six MockMvc tests carry genuine negative assertions that would catch the likely regressions: a veterinarian holding no specialty absent from the rendered page, no active navigation entry, and no link to the route in the shared navigation. ClinicServiceTests adds a real-I/O test proving the JPQL ORDER BY against seeded data. All four message keys the template uses already exist in all ten populated bundles, verified directly, so the build-time i18n sync test genuinely covers the language criterion. The one gap is small: no test asserts what renders in the cell for an unheld specialty, only that the row exists.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round 2 is clean for all three reviewers the risk-proportional plan dispatched, with empty findings. The hedge is in the security reviewer's round-1 approval, which is the only round it ran and which carries two parked recommendations: it states plainly that supply chain was not verified against the NVD and calls that a gap in coverage rather than a clean result, leaving the standing Spring Boot 4.1.0 framework-CVE check to a human or CI; and it notes that system-design.md Security Context and Threat Model were not extended to name the new route, even though this slice edits that document. Neither reached a finding, so nobody closed either, and this facet is where they reach the human.

scope_deviation.note: Zero consultations, zero build retries, and the single design revision was bookkeeping: a superseding design-block adding two doc paths the first record's prose described but its path list omitted, which is what tripped the autofix audit. The change departs from the prd-entry file targets by adding a separate SpecialtyController rather than extending VetController and by touching no message bundle, but the design-block decided both explicitly and for stated reasons. Every non-goal holds: no navigation entry, no link from another page, no pagination, no search, no management surface.

rationale: Read every hunk; the derivation, template, and query are contained, additive, and behave as described, with unusually real tests. Nothing here needs a careful correctness read. What does need a human is the security reviewer's parked pair: the supply-chain check was never run, and the new route is absent from the Security Context and Threat Model this slice already edits.
